subject: Clarifying data custody expectations for Dedicated vs Private VPC — AtlasRetail follow-up
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Subject: Clarifying data custody expectations for Dedicated vs Private VPC — AtlasRetail follow-up

Hi Samir / Nina — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and requests so we can align the next steps with your security & procurement teams. I pulled the key points from our conversation below and added a short set of asks for the security deep-dive we'll schedule.

Call recap (short):
- AtlasRetail is evaluating Redwood to power real-time product recommendations and checkout fraud checks (POC scope).
- Primary concern: hard requirement for control over where production inference data and logs live (no persistent storage of raw PII outside customer boundary).
- Initial preference leaned toward Dedicated for performance predictability, but security team is pushing for a Private VPC/control-plane deployment.

Specific clarifying questions we promised to confirm:
1) "Dedicated" option: does Redwood offer a Dedicated capacity deployment that can be placed inside the customer's VPC, or is Dedicated always Redwood-managed network-wise?
2) KMS: must keys be customer-managed (BYOK/HSM)? If so, can we integrate with Azure Key Vault + customer HSM per your notes?
3) Logs & telemetry: can we provide a configuration that redacts or prevents retention of raw request/response bodies (only token-level metrics retained)?
4) Egress & IP controls: can we support strict egress allowlists and private peering to AtlasRetail networks?

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Please confirm which of the items above are must-haves vs nice-to-haves for procurement. A quick reply inline would be great.
- Security deep-dive: propose Tue Jul 24, 10:00–11:00 PT. Laura (ops) and Karthik (solutions) will present architecture options and a checklist. Can you confirm who from your security and procurement teams should join?
- I'll attach our one-pager that shows the differences between Dedicated, Dedicated-in-VPC (if applicable), and Private VPC/control plane — see attachment.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-private-onepager.pdf (one-pager), will follow up with a technical checklist if we confirm the deep-dive.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@atlasretail.com>

Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@atlasretail.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@atlasretail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying data custody expectations for Dedicated vs Private VPC — AtlasRetail follow-up

Soojin — thanks for the recap, very helpful. Short answers below and a couple of follow-ups from our side.

Inline:
1) Dedicated placement: our security stance today is that any production inference handling raw customer PII must be within our VPC or on-prem. So the Dedicated option only works if it can be deployed so that inference nodes and disk buffers are inside our network boundary. If Dedicated is strictly Redwood-managed networking, that won't pass.
2) KMS: must be customer-managed keys (BYOK). We prefer Azure Key Vault with our HSM.
3) Logs: we cannot have raw request/response bodies stored or searchable outside our environment. Token-level aggregate metrics are fine, and we will accept a telemetry stream that we ingest into our SIEM if needed.
4) Egress: yes — private peering and a static allowlist are required.

Procurement asks:
- Please provide an estimate of the monthly delta between "Dedicated in our VPC" (if that's supported) vs "Private VPC (control plane in customer network)". We need a ballpark for our internal TCO discussion.
- If Dedicated-in-VPC is not supported, highlight what changes (control-plane residency, admin access, support model) when moving to Private.

I attached our security checklist (AtlasSecurityReqs.xlsx) for reference.

Samir
Director, Platform Security
AtlasRetail

[Attachment: AtlasSecurityReqs.xlsx]

Subject: Re: Clarifying data custody expectations for Dedicated vs Private VPC — AtlasRetail follow-up

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear answers and the checklist. I wanted to make sure we use consistent terminology and give you an operational checklist before the deep-dive.

Terminology note (short):
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved compute capacity that we operate; network tenancy is Redwood-managed by default. It provides tenant isolation at the orchestration layer but runs in Redwood's VPCs.
- Redwood Dedicated-in-Customer-VPC: this is an engineered deployment we can evaluate as a Customer VPC deployment model — operationally similar to Private but with reserved capacity. It's not our default SKU and requires an implementation review (networking, deployment automation, support boundaries).
- Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem): control plane and serving plane are deployed into customer-managed networking; Redwood provides installers and an ops integration path (BYOK, private peering, no egress of raw payloads).

Based on AtlasRetail requirements (BYOK, no persistent raw PII outside your boundary, private peering), the safe prescriptive path is Redwood Private. That said, we can propose a scoped "Dedicated-in-Customer-VPC" pilot if you prefer the semantics of reserved capacity with tighter price delta than full Private (we'd surface a technical design and run an implementation feasibility study).

Suggested mutual action plan (MAP) — propose we capture this during the deep-dive:
- Week 0 (this week): confirm participants from AtlasRetail security & procurement. (Samir: who should join?)
- Week 1: security deep-dive (Laura + infra) — architecture options (Private vs Dedicated-in-Customer-VPC), KMS integration design, logging/retention config.
- Week 2: draft implementation plan & price comparison (Redwood to provide pilot SOW and a TCO sketch for both options).
- Week 3: procurement review and pilot contract (if agreed).

Deliverables we will prepare before the deep-dive:
- Short design note comparing Private vs Dedicated-in-Customer-VPC (network diagrams, responsibilities).
- KMS integration spec (support for Azure Key Vault + HSM flow).
- Logging/telemetry options and a retention/redaction configuration template.

I'll attach the one-pager again and will circulate the design note before the Tue deep-dive if we confirm participants.

Thanks — Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
